notFound: We couldn't identify this medicine with confidence. A pharmacist can tell you what it contains.
disclaimer: Information only, not medical advice. Check with your pharmacist or doctor.
uses.headline: For {uses}
stripRead.title: Read from the strip
stripRead.body: This brand isn't in our database yet. The ingredients were read from the composition printed on the strip, so compare them with the strip.
incomplete.title: Some ingredients may be missing
incomplete.body: Our data lists only part of this medicine's ingredients. The strip shows the full list.
ban.exact.title: Banned in India
ban.exact.body: The Government of India has banned this combination. A pharmacist can suggest an alternative.
ban.related.title: A similar combination is banned
ban.related.body: "{title}" is banned. Yours looks like a different form or strength, which a pharmacist can confirm.
abx.title: Antibiotic, WHO {group} group
abx.access.body: Access antibiotics are the first choice for common infections. They work only on bacteria, not on colds or flu.
abx.watch.body: Watch antibiotics carry a higher risk of resistance, so they are kept for specific infections on a doctor's prescription.
abx.reserve.body: Reserve antibiotics are the last option for infections that other antibiotics can't treat.
abx.course.title: The full course matters
abx.course.body: Stopping early lets surviving bacteria return stronger. Saving leftovers for later or sharing them is a common cause of resistance.
abx.local.title: Antibiotic for local use
abx.local.body: Contains {names}, used on the skin, eye or ear.
abx.whoNotRec.title: WHO does not recommend this combination
abx.whoNotRec.body: There is no good evidence for fixed-dose combinations like {title}. A doctor can explain the alternatives.
dup.title: Also in your {product}
dup.body: Both contain {ingredient}, so taking both doubles the dose. A pharmacist can tell you which one to take.
ix.title: {severity} interaction with {product}
ix.body: {a} and {b} can affect each other. A pharmacist can check whether both are safe together.
generic.title: Jan Aushadhi generic
expiry.soon.title: Expires in {days} days
expiry.expired.title: Expired
course.title: Antibiotic course
course.dialogBody: Enter what the doctor prescribed. AMRit reminds you until the course is complete.
home.subtitle: Your family's medicines, checked
home.scanBody: What it's for, whether it's safe with your other medicines, and a cheaper generic.
home.allClearBody: Add the medicines you take and AMRit checks them together.
home.awareness: World AMR Awareness Week, 18 to 24 November
profile.name: Name
meds.title: {name}'s medicines
meds.emptyBody: Scan a strip or search by name, then add it here.
scan.hint: Hold the strip steady with the name in the frame
scan.glare: Tilt it slightly if light reflects off the foil
scan.permission: AMRit needs the camera to read strips. You can also pick a photo or search by name.
res.ttsMissing: This language's voice isn't installed on your phone. Settings › System › Languages › Text-to-speech.
conf.title: Which one is it?
conf.sub: These match what we read. Tap the one whose name is on the strip.
nf.title: Not identified
nf.tip1: Tilt the strip so light doesn't shine straight off the foil
nf.tip2: Fill the frame with the side that shows the name and composition
nf.tip3: Tap to focus, and use the torch in dim light
search.title: Search
search.tip: Try a brand like Dolo, Augmentin or Pan-D
onb.title: Know every medicine in your home
onb.privacy1: No account and no name. Photos stay on your phone unless a strip is too hard to read.
onb.privacy2: Each scan shares only the ingredients, the antibiotic group, whether it is banned, your pincode and the hour.
onb.privacy3: That helps health teams map antibiotic use in India.
settings.title: Settings
settings.languageBeta: Machine-translated, a native speaker hasn't checked these yet
settings.pincodeWhy: Used only to show antibiotic use by area. Never linked to you.
settings.privacy: No account. Photos stay on your phone; only anonymous medicine data is shared.
settings.sources: Sources: Indian medicine data, WHO AWaRe 2025, CDSCO, DDInter and Jan Aushadhi.
nf.ayush.title: Ayurvedic or homoeopathic medicine
nf.ayush.body: This pack is labelled as an AYUSH medicine. AMRit checks allopathic medicines only, so it was not checked. A pharmacist or AYUSH doctor can advise on it.
res.qr.mismatch.title: The pack's QR code names a different medicine
res.qr.mismatch.body: QR code: {brand}. The printed name and the QR code should match. Ask the pharmacist to check this pack before using it.
res.alert.spurious.title: This batch was reported as fake (spurious)
res.alert.nsq.title: This batch failed a government quality test
res.alert.body: Batch {batch}: {result}. Reported by {by}, {month}. Don't take it; return it to the pharmacist.
notif.alert.title: Check your {product}
notif.alert.body: {kind}. Batch {batch}, CDSCO alert {month}. Don't take it; return it to the pharmacist.
scan.closer: Move closer so the small print fills the frame
scan.flip: Turn the strip over: the composition is printed on the back
res.leftover.title: You already have this antibiotic from before
res.leftover.body: Saved on {date}, with no course running. Leftover antibiotics shouldn't be taken for a new illness or given to someone else: the medicine or the number of doses may be wrong, and that helps bacteria become resistant. Ask a doctor first.
res.dispose.title: Getting rid of leftover antibiotics
res.dispose.body: Don't flush them or throw them loose in the bin. Give them back at a pharmacy that takes back unused medicines, or ask the pharmacist how to dispose of them.
notif.course.title: Time for your {antibiotic} dose
notif.course.body: {taken} of {total} doses logged. Finish the full course even if you feel better.
notif.expiry.title: {product} expires {date}
notif.expired.title: {product} has expired
notif.expiry.body: Don't use it after expiry. A pharmacist can tell you how to dispose of it.
rx.question: Did you get this antibiotic with a doctor's prescription?
rx.private: Your answer is anonymous. Only the medicine group, your area pincode and the hour are recorded, to map antibiotic sales without prescription.
rx.noBody: In India antibiotics are prescription-only medicines, so a pharmacy shouldn't sell them without one. A doctor can tell you whether you need this antibiotic at all.
settings.largeSub: Bigger letters and buttons across the app
settings.autoReadSub: Each scan result is read out as soon as it appears
seen.title: What we read
seen.sub: From the photo of your strip. The photo is not saved.
seen.hint: Something misread? Tap it to search for the right medicine.
box.expired.title: {product} expired in {date}
box.expired.body: Don't take it. Give it back at a pharmacy that takes back old medicines.
box.recalled.title: {product}: {what}
box.banned.title: {product} is banned in India
box.leftover.title: {product} is a leftover antibiotic
box.leftover.body: Don't take it for a new illness or give it to someone else without a doctor. The wrong antibiotic, or too few doses, helps bacteria become resistant.
box.ctaSub: Scan every strip at home, one after another. We find what's expired, recalled, doubled up or left over.
box.hintScan: Show the strips one at a time. Each is added as soon as it's read.
box.title: Your medicine box
box.subtitle: {n} medicines, {name}
box.empty: No strips yet. Point the camera at a strip; it's added when it's read.
box.unknown: {n} strips couldn't be identified. Scan them on their own, or search by name.
box.summary: {bin} to throw away, {ask} to ask about, {fine} fine
box.dispose.title: How to get rid of them
box.dispose.body: Don't flush medicines or throw them loose in the bin. Give them back at a pharmacy that takes back unused medicines, or ask the pharmacist how to dispose of them.
passport.insight.watch: {n} Watch or Reserve antibiotics in the last 3 months. Show this to your doctor before the next antibiotic.
passport.insight.stopped: A course was stopped early this year. Stopping early lets surviving bacteria come back stronger; ask your doctor before stopping.
passport.insight.noRx: An antibiotic was taken without a doctor's prescription this year. Antibiotics should only be taken when a doctor prescribes them.
passport.insight.many: {n} antibiotic courses in the last year. That's worth talking over with your doctor.
passport.title: Antibiotic passport
passport.intro: Every antibiotic course, and antibiotics kept at home. Doctors ask what you've taken before; this is the answer.
passport.empty: No antibiotics recorded for {name} yet. Scan an antibiotic and track its course, and it appears here.
passport.ended: Course days over: {done} of {total} doses ticked
passport.inHouse: Kept at home, no course started
passport.private: Kept only on this phone. It leaves only if you share it.
doctor.title: Antibiotic history (kept by the patient in AMRit)
doctor.period: Newest first. WHO AWaRe group shown for each.
doctor.none: No antibiotics recorded in the last 12 months
doctor.note: Recorded by the patient from medicine strips scanned in the AMRit app. Not verified by a clinician.
near.ctaSub: What AMRit users across India are buying, anonymously. Every antibiotic you scan adds to it.
near.title: Antibiotics near you
near.none: No data yet. Connect to the internet and try again.
near.heroBody: out of {total} medicine scans, all anonymous
near.watchBody: WHO keeps these for specific infections because resistance to them is a bigger risk.
near.rxBody: From {n} anonymous answers to “Did you get this with a prescription?”
near.rxNotYet: The prescription share appears once {k} people have answered.
near.privacy: Only the medicine group, a 3-digit area code and the hour are recorded for each scan. Areas appear only with {k} or more scans.
resist.title: What ICMR found in Indian hospitals (2024)
resist.row.urine: Urine infections (E. coli): {pct} still responded to {drug} ({s} of {n} tested)
resist.row.typhoid: Typhoid (Salmonella Typhi, blood): {pct} still responded to {drug} ({s} of {n} tested)
resist.row.staph: Staph infections (S. aureus): {pct} still responded to {drug} ({s} of {n} tested)
resist.note: This is hospital surveillance across India, not a test of your infection. Only a doctor can choose the right antibiotic.
resist.source: ICMR AMR Surveillance Network, Annual Report 2024, p. {pages}
bill.ctaSub: Photograph a printed bill: see what you'd save at Jan Aushadhi, and if the medicines are safe together.
bill.title: Pharmacy bill check
bill.intro: Take a photo of a printed pharmacy bill. Each medicine on it is matched, priced against its Jan Aushadhi generic, and checked against the others on the bill.
bill.photo: Take a photo of the bill
bill.privacy: The photo is read on this phone and then deleted. Handwritten prescriptions can't be read.
bill.none: No medicines could be matched on this bill. Make sure it's a printed bill, flat and well lit, and try again.
bill.saveBody: {pct}% less at a Jan Aushadhi Kendra: {generic} instead of {brand} for the medicines that have a generic.
bill.noGeneric: None of these medicines has a Jan Aushadhi generic in our list.
bill.noGenericLine: No Jan Aushadhi generic in our list
bill.unrecognisedBody: These lines weren't matched to a medicine, so they aren't counted. Scan the strip itself to check one.
bill.priceSource: Estimate. Generic prices are from Jan Aushadhi's published list (PMBI, April 2025); bill prices as printed.
bill.abxBody: Take it only as your doctor prescribed, and finish the course.
alt.title: Same medicine, other brands
alt.sub: {n} brands with the same salt, strength and form. Ask your pharmacist before switching.
alt.priceNote: MRPs from the medicine dataset; shop prices vary.
alt.locator: Official Jan Aushadhi Kendra finder (by PIN code)
